purpose: Read-only orchestration view across canonical Shine Defence review and certification state, identifying the exact guarded helper appropriate for the next workflow step without executing it.
scope: Review workflow state comes from review-queue-v1.
Canonical certification state comes from the reviewed ecosystem ledger, exact receipt presence and revocation ledger.
The controller does not infer the commit currently deployed by an application; deployment freshness still requires app/deployment-specific release-status evaluation.
rules: Every known app appears exactly once in deterministic app-id order.
A pending review candidate takes workflow precedence over idle certification state.
Human-required review-queue actions remain explicitly human-required and are never converted into executable automation.
Approved checklist states route only to the existing guarded first-certification or re-certification helpers.
Human-rejected pending reviews route only to the guarded rejection finalizer.

A reviewed app with no pending candidate and an active revocation on its exact reviewed commit/profile is reported as reviewed_release_revoked and requires a new release candidate before badge restoration.
A reviewed app with no pending candidate, no matching revocation and an exact receipt file is canonical_reviewed_idle.
Missing canonical receipt state is blocked rather than automatically repaired.
An app known only through finalized candidate history and absent from the reviewed ledger is uncertified_idle and may begin again through candidate intake.
The controller returns helper paths and arguments as recommendations only; it never invokes a mutating helper.
JSON output is deterministic and suitable for future dashboards or external orchestration.
When a valid latest deployment observation exists, observed deployment status takes precedence over idle canonical certification state.
A canonical revocation on the reviewed release does not label a different observed deployment as revoked; the observed commit/profile is evaluated through release-status-v1.
Apps without deployment observations remain explicitly unobserved and are routed to the deployment-observation recorder rather than guessed.
nonClaims: The controller is not certification authority.
canonical_reviewed_idle does not prove that the reviewed commit is the commit currently deployed.
A recommended helper has not been executed merely because it appears in controller output.
The controller does not replace human checklist decisions.
An absent deployment observation is not evidence that the reviewed release is currently deployed.
